behaviors.summary: Boolean environment values accept only exact lowercase true or false; absence uses each declared default.
Integer values use Number.parseInt base 10, reject non-finite results, and enforce per-setting bounds; trailing non-numeric text is therefore accepted after an integer prefix.
AGENT_ROLE_URL is required and http/https-only; ENABLED_SKILLS is a trimmed comma-separated list whose nonempty entries are individually http/https-only.
ALLOWED_SKILL_DOMAINS is comma-split, trimmed, lowercased, de-duplicated in insertion order, and defaults to an empty allow-all list.
Enabled Teams requires both Microsoft credentials; enabled Telegram requires its token; enabled Discord requires its token; enabled WhatsApp requires verify, access, and phone-number tokens.

Runtime defaults are port 3978, info logging, 3600000 ms session TTL, 100 sessions, gpt-4o, 30000 ms skill timeout, 120000 ms SDK timeout, rate 30, localhost domain, and false auto-update/trust-proxy.
A nonempty trimmed GITHUB_TOKEN activates the Copilot engine during startup; without a PAT, Device Flow must be enabled.
Token activation starts and pings a replacement engine before swapping it in, then stops the previous engine; concurrent activations serialize through the current switch promise.
Device Flow POSTs JSON to GitHub's device-code endpoint with scope copilot, Accept application/json, and a 15-second timeout.
A pending unexpired user code is reused; instructions contain the verification URI and bold user code, while startup failures become a user-facing failure string rather than a rejection.
Token polling starts after GitHub's interval, retries non-OK responses and unexpected errors, adds five seconds for slow_down, and clears state for expiry or access denial.
On access_token, the runtime fetches /user with Bearer auth, falls back to login unknown on any failure, clears pending state, and activates the engine.
Role fetch uses a 10-second timeout, accepts JSON or text/plain, rejects non-2xx responses, enforces a 1 MiB content-length byte hint and a 1 MiB JavaScript-character body limit.

JSON role parsing is attempted for JSON content types or bodies beginning with {; a string content field takes precedence over prompt, a non-string or absent content falls back to prompt, and the selected value must be nonempty.
A string model is returned unchanged; unknown models only emit a warning and are still attempted.
JSON-content-type parse or validation errors are fatal, while equivalent errors for text content fall through and use the entire raw body verbatim as a model-less system prompt.

A legacy skill must be an object with a safe identifier name, nonempty description, non-null JavaScript-object parameters value (including arrays), and nonempty executeCode string; extra fields are ignored.

Skill URLs fetch concurrently with a 10-second timeout and Accept application/json; non-2xx, parse, validation, and bodies over 524288 characters are logged and skipped independently while successful skills retain input order.
Legacy execution prefers isolated-vm with a 128 MiB isolate; node:vm is an explicit reduced-isolation development fallback, and production startup fails when isolated-vm is unavailable.
Registration appends name/code pairs without duplicate rejection; execution rejects disposed executors and unknown names, and duplicate lookup resolves the first registered name.
An empty domain list allows all URLs; otherwise URL parsing must succeed and the lowercase hostname must equal or be a subdomain of an allowed entry.

httpGet and httpPost require string URLs, enforce domain policy, apply the skill timeout to fetch, and return response text without rejecting HTTP error status codes; httpPost forwards body and headers.
log stringifies input, truncates to 2000 characters, and writes a structured skill-tagged info event.
Legacy code is interpolated as a function and invoked with params and bridge APIs in node:vm or isolated-vm; this evaluation behavior is intentionally absent from the final product.
Executor disposal is idempotent, marks the executor unusable, and disposes the isolate when present.
Session get refreshes lastAccess; set records Date.now and updates existing conversation IDs without capacity eviction.
Adding a new session at or above capacity removes the entry with the smallest lastAccess timestamp before insertion.
An unref'd 60-second timer removes entries whose idle age is strictly greater than SESSION_TTL_MS and logs only when at least one expires.
Reload clear removes all map entries but retains the cleanup timer; destroyAll also clears the timer. Legacy removal does not individually stop SDK session objects.
The Copilot client uses the selected GitHub token with autoRestart true; start must be followed by a successful ping or engine activation fails.

A missing conversation session is created with the role model or default model, replacement system message, current tools, infinite sessions, approveAll permissions, and the conversation ID as session ID.
Pre-tool hooks deny names absent from the current tool list and allow known names; post-use and session errors are logged, and session error handling returns skip.
sendAndWait uses SDK_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS; missing content returns (No response from AI), while thrown errors are logged and converted to the fixed retry apology.

Only one reload runs at a time; role reload failure aborts, ordinary per-skill fetch/parse failures produce a fulfilled partial or empty replacement list, only a whole loadSkills rejection retains prior skills, and executor registration failure disposes only the replacement.
Successful engine reload replaces role and tools and clears every active session so new role/tool state applies on the next message.

Reload does not synchronize with an in-flight createSession call; a creation started with the old role/tools can finish after clear and reinsert stale session state. The Rust shim uses generation fencing to prevent this race.
GET / always returns 200 service/status/auth/channel metadata, advertises only health/device/chat endpoints, and conditionally appends authentication and no-channel tips.
GET /health always returns 200 status ok with floored process-relative uptime, current skill/session/model/auth/device-flow/channel fields, including while unauthenticated.
GET /auth/device returns 200 already-authenticated, 400 when disabled, 200 with auth_instructions when enabled, or 500 for an unexpected getAuthMessage rejection.
POST /chat selects the first string among message, text, and prompt, trims it, selects conversation_id before conversationId before http-<remoteAddress>, and returns 400 for empty input.
/help and /start return fixed help with 200 before authentication; other unauthenticated requests return 401 with Device Flow instructions when available or a token/device-flow error otherwise.
Authenticated chat returns 200 {reply}; an unexpected engine.chat rejection returns 500 {error: Internal error}.
POST /api/messages and its Bot Framework adapter exist only when Teams is enabled; adapter turn errors log and send a fixed generic retry message.
GET and POST are registered at the configured WhatsApp path only when a handler exists.
POST /admin/reload exists only for nonempty ADMIN_TOKEN plus reloadFn, requires an exact Bearer token even from loopback, and returns 200 result, 409 concurrent reload, or 500 generic failure.
System and exec routes exist only for nonempty ADMIN_TOKEN and accept either an exact Bearer token or remote address 127.0.0.1, ::1, or ::ffff:127.0.0.1.
GET /admin/system returns 403 when unauthorized or 200 with process version/PID/floored uptime/rounded MiB memory and host/platform/arch/CPU/memory/uptime/load average.
POST /admin/exec permits only uptime, disk, memory, top, docker_ps, docker_stats, docker_images, docker_logs, netstat, who, hostname, and date with fixed executable/argument specifications.

Unknown actions return 400 plus the ordered allow-list; docker_logs target strips characters outside letters, digits, underscore, hyphen, and dot; execFile has a 15-second timeout and 1 MiB buffer, and both command success and failure return HTTP 200 with bounded text fields.
The in-memory per-IP token bucket starts with max-1 after the first accepted request, refills continuously at max/60000 per millisecond, caps at max, and has no bucket eviction.
Only URL strings beginning /api/messages are limited; trusted proxy mode uses the first x-forwarded-for value, otherwise socket remoteAddress, and denial returns 429 {error: Too many requests}.

Telegram, Discord, and WhatsApp trim incoming text, ignore empty messages, return Device Flow instructions or a fixed unconfigured string without an engine, and convert unexpected processing errors to a fixed apology.

Teams ignores empty text, provides an authentication hint without an engine, drops messages without conversation ID, sends a typing activity, chats by conversation ID, and sends a fixed apology if processing throws.
New non-bot members receive a fixed greeting, and edited messages are processed as new messages.
Telegram repeatedly calls getUpdates with timeout=25, allowed_updates=[message], optional offset, and a 35-second request timeout; failures are logged and the loop waits pollIntervalMs.
Offsets advance before handling each update; non-text/blank messages are ignored, username falls back to joined first/last name then telegram-user, and conversation ID is telegram:<chat.id>.
Nonempty replies are split at 4000 characters and POSTed sequentially to sendMessage with disabled link previews and 10-second timeouts; any non-2xx throws with status.
Discord opens the configured gateway, logs open/error/close, reconnects three seconds after close while running, and stop cancels timers, removes listeners, and closes the socket.

Gateway sequence is updated from packets; HELLO starts interval heartbeats and IDENTIFY, dispatch is handled, reconnect/invalid-session closes the socket, heartbeat ACK and unknown operations are ignored.
IDENTIFY sends the bot token, configured intents, process platform, and gta-claw browser/device labels; sends are dropped unless the socket is OPEN.
READY stores/logs the session ID; only nonblank non-bot MESSAGE_CREATE events are processed, with conversation ID discord:<channel_id>:<author.id> and username as userName.
Replies are split at 1900 characters and POSTed sequentially to Discord v10 with Bot authorization and 10-second timeouts; non-2xx errors include status, status text, and response body.

The async gateway message listener has no local catch, so malformed JSON and rejected message processing or outbound sends can escape as listener promise rejections; the Rust shim logs and contains these failures.
WhatsApp verification requires subscribe mode, exact verify token, and nonempty challenge, returning the raw challenge as text/plain 200 or JSON Forbidden 403.
Webhook entries, changes, and messages are processed sequentially; only nonblank text messages run, using whatsapp:<from> as conversation ID and the sender number as userName.
The webhook waits for processing and outbound sends before replying 200 {ok:true}; any error logs and returns 500 {error: Webhook handling failed}.
Replies are split at 3500 characters and POSTed sequentially to Graph API v20.0 with Bearer access token and 10-second timeout; non-2xx errors include status, status text, and body.

Text at or below the limit is unchanged; longer text prefers the last newline after half the limit, then space after 30 percent, otherwise hard-splits, and trimStart is applied only to the remaining suffix.
Teams and Telegram use 4000-character chunks, Discord 1900, and WhatsApp 3500; chunks send sequentially and stop on the first send error.

Proxy precedence is HTTPS_PROXY, https_proxy, HTTP_PROXY, http_proxy, ALL_PROXY, all_proxy; absence logs debug, and successful setup installs a global dispatcher with credentials redacted from the info log.
Invalid proxy construction logs the full configured proxy alongside the error and startup continues using the existing dispatcher.
Pino is initialized at module load with LOG_LEVEL or info; exact NODE_ENV=development uses pino/file to stdout, otherwise default transport behavior applies.

Installed SDK version reads its package JSON, latest SDK uses the npm latest endpoint, installed CLI executes --version with a five-second timeout, and latest CLI uses the GitHub releases endpoint; every probe degrades to unknown.
SDK and CLI probes run concurrently; updateAvailable is simple non-unknown string inequality rather than semantic-version ordering, and results/warnings are logged.
The startup update check is launched without blocking service readiness, and top-level failure is logged as a warning.
AUTO_UPDATE=true is rejected during configuration; dependency and CLI updates must change reviewed lockfiles instead of invoking npm or a curl-to-shell installer.
SIGTERM and SIGINT share one shutdown promise; repeated signals log and return the same in-progress promise.
Shutdown initiates server close, stops Device Flow, awaits Telegram then Discord then engine, disposes the executor, logs clean shutdown, and exits 0; fatal startup logs and exits 1.

The digest-pinned Node 26 builder copies exact package roots, runs npm ci with scripts disabled, explicitly rebuilds only isolated-vm and koffi, compiles TypeScript with the locked local tool, and prunes development dependencies without scripts.

The runtime reuses the pinned Node 26 digest, copies the built app, production dependencies, and both package roots, uses the SDK-locked Copilot CLI, requires production isolation, runs as user node, health-checks /health, and starts dist/index.js.

run.sh config mode strips comments/blank lines and CR characters into mode-600 .env, requires role URL and conditional Teams credentials, validates selected booleans/URLs/rate/image/auth/channels, and deletes invalid generated env files for initial required-field failures.

Interactive setup defaults to Chinese, Device Flow, no channels, gpt-4o, localhost, image aizhihuxiao/gta-claw:latest, rate 30, and disabled updates/trusted proxy, then writes all runtime values to .env.

Deploy prefers a local image then attempts pull, otherwise pulls or builds from the local parent repo or a depth-one GitHub clone; it replaces container gta-claw, uses restart unless-stopped and .env, always maps 3978:3978, and polls container health/status up to 60 seconds.

--update pulls or rebuilds then recreates the container; --stop force-removes it; --status shows docker state and host then container health JSON; --logs follows the last 100 lines; default auto-loads conf/gta-claw.conf or starts interactive setup.

Publishing also performs a secret-free pull-request build; actions are SHA-pinned, one amd64 image is built and validated by image ID, lockfile, CLI, and isolation checks, then authenticated events push every generated tag only when registry digests agree.
The bundled claw-steward role is a valid content/model role using claude-opus-4.6 and remains a data asset.
The repository bundles ten legacy executeCode examples; each is inventoried with recognized bridges and requires a manual Rust/WASI port before activation.
